# land_group

Lands changes (1 to 32, each a head with an optional base and idempotency\_key) in order onto target, main by default, as one operation: each merged onto what the clean ones before it make, as land\_check plans them, the clean ones a chain of landed changesets with one move of target. A conflicting change is reported (items\[\].report) and passed over; with none clean it is E\_NOTHING\_TO\_LAND, each outcome in details.items. Give each change an idempotency\_key to make a retry safe.

```yaml
title: "land_group"
description: "Land a group."
since: "0.11.0"
mutates: true
identity_required: true
cli_command: "swarmops land-group"
envelope_op: "land_group"
request_type: "LandGroupReq"
annotations: {"destructiveHint":false,"idempotentHint":true,"openWorldHint":false,"readOnlyHint":false}
max_result_chars: null
```

## Input schema

`arguments` is a `LandGroupReq`: `swarmops schema LandGroupReq` prints the type. A field the type does not know is ignored.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `changes` | array of object | yes |  | The changes, in the order they land: 1 to 32 (`E_INVALID_ARG` for none, `E_TOO_LARGE` past 32), each key once. |
| `max_attempts` | integer | no | `8` | How many times the group plans and publishes at most before `E_CAS_RETRY_EXHAUSTED`: 1 to 32. |
| `max_conflict_bytes` | integer | no | `32768` | The most bytes of hunk text each conflicting change's report carries, as a land's. |
| `target` | string | no | `"main"` | The ref the changes land on: `main` or `release/<name>`, which must exist. |

## Annotations

It adds a changeset onto a ref's head and moves the ref to it, keeping all the ref held. Run again with the same arguments, it finds its change on the ref and adds nothing: `replayed` with an `idempotency_key`, `E_NOTHING_TO_LAND` without.

| Annotation | Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `destructiveHint` | `false` | True: a tool that changes the store may overwrite or delete what is there, not only add to it. |
| `idempotentHint` | `true` | True: calling it again with the same arguments changes nothing more. |
| `openWorldHint` | `false` | True: it reaches beyond a closed set of things. Every tool here stays inside the store. |
| `readOnlyHint` | `false` | True: the tool does not change its environment, the store. |

Its entry in `tools/list` carries no `_meta`.

## CLI command

[`swarmops land-group`](../commands/land-group.md) runs the same operation and prints the same envelope.

## Examples

```json
{
  "id": 44,
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "method": "tools/call",
  "params": {
    "arguments": {
      "changes": [
        {
          "head": "[one]",
          "idempotency_key": "group-1"
        },
        {
          "head": "[two]",
          "idempotency_key": "group-2"
        }
      ]
    },
    "name": "land_group"
  }
}
```

The server ran as `swarmops mcp --repo [tmp]/store --as agent/worker-17`, after `initialize`. Recorded by the MCP tests. A name in square brackets, such as `[tmp]` or `[c1]`, stands for what differs from run to run: the test's temporary directory, an id, a time, the version.

## Return information

A tool result: the envelope, whose `op` is `land_group`, as `structuredContent` and again as the text of its one `content` block. `isError` is true exactly when the envelope's `ok` is false. On success the envelope's `result` is what [`swarmops land-group`](../commands/land-group.md#return-information) returns.

## Errors

A failed call is a tool result with `isError: true`; the envelope's `error.code` is one of the [error codes](../errors.md).

- [`E_INVALID_ARG`](../errors.md#e_invalid_arg): arguments that do not fit `LandGroupReq`, a field named twice among them included, or that break one of the server's own rules.
- [`E_IDENTITY_REQUIRED`](../errors.md#e_identity_required): the server runs with no identity.
- [`E_NOT_A_REPO`](../errors.md#e_not_a_repo): the server's store is not there; the server serves on.
- [`E_INTERNAL`](../errors.md#e_internal): the operation panicked, a bug.

Then the errors of the operation, as [`swarmops land-group`](../commands/land-group.md#errors) lists them.
